task: NAME the low-nibble-0x2 family (integer/float register-operand compare-SELECT + compact/length-only residue); the single biggest family-only chunk (byte0 0x22 dominant).

descriptors.semantics: d = (predicate) ? srcA : srcB  ; register-operand integer/float compare-SELECT, NARROW 8-byte form (both sources are registers, no trailing operand word). byte0 low-nibble 2 = group; byte0 HIGH nibble = dst r0..r15; byte+1 = srcA/size descriptor; byte+2 low 3 bits == 0b111 identifies the register-select forms (op variants 0x07/0x0f/0x1f/0x27/0x2f in byte+2, upper 5 bits = opsel); byte+3 = srcA, byte+4 = srcB. This is the DOMINANT low-nibble-2 form (own-MSL: emitted for int/float ternaries and the quotient/remainder correction SELECT in integer division). The 0x25 8-byte sibling (isel_reg8) and 0x2f 10-byte sibling (isel_reg) were already named; this generalises the same family. Predicate/condition source is byte+1/byte+2-encoded (not reconstructed per-bit here -- the SELECT choice itself is the documented hardware op).
descriptors.provenance: OWN-MSL byte-diff (EXP-M4-13 R5): `(a>b)?a:b` (int) compiles to `12 81 27 85 01 84 07 20` (8B, dst r1); `(a>b)?a:b` variants and `a/b` correction to `02 93 27 0f 86 14 00 02` -- all 8-byte low-nibble-2 with byte+2 low3==7, cleanly bracketed by iadd2/carry_gen/n2_op6. dst=byte0-hi inherits the family reg-sweep (iminmax provenance). byte+2 confirmed a SELECT (not imad) because own-MSL `a*b+c` (int) emits the 12-byte 0x9f imad instead. NOT HW-dispatch validated (M4 compile-only).

descriptors.semantics: d = (predicate) ? srcA : srcB  ; register-operand compare-SELECT, WIDE 10-byte form -- the isel8 sibling that carries a trailing operand word (byte+8:9), used when srcB (or the correction addend) is an immediate / wide operand. byte+2 low 3 bits == 0b111 (op variants 0x07/0x0f/0x1f/0x27/0x3f/0x5f/0x67/0x7f in byte+2). The already-named 0x2f form (isel_reg) and the 0x27/0x81/0x22 form (rt_transform_test) are more-specific and still win the decode; this names the remaining low3==7 10-byte selects. NOTE: a small number of byte0==0x22 low3==7 instances (notably byte+2==0x9f) may be an over-read of the byte0==0x22 default-to-10 length rule rather than a genuine 10-byte select -- see UNRESOLVED. Operand semantics beyond the register SELECT are left structural (rule 5).
descriptors.provenance: OWN-MSL byte-diff (EXP-M4-13 R5): int div/mod correction emits `22 8f 07 91 22 80 05 00 80 06` and `72 81 27 80 22 20 07 c2 20 80` (10B, byte+2 low3==7, trailing operand word), cleanly bracketed by carry_gen. dst=byte0-hi from the family reg-sweep. Same SELECT semantics as isel8 (confirmed vs 0x9f imad). NOT HW-dispatch validated.

descriptors.semantics: d = (predicate) ? srcA : srcB  ; register/immediate-operand compare-SELECT, WIDE 10-byte form with byte+2 low 3 bits == 0b101 (op variants 0x05/0x0d/0x15/0x25/0x2d). 0x25 = the wide (immediate-srcB) select; 0x2d = the integer division/modulo QUOTIENT correction select. Sibling of the 8-byte 0x25 isel_reg8. Same dst=byte0-hi family model. A few byte0==0x22 instances (0x05/0x15) may be over-reads of the 0x22 default-to-10 length rule (UNRESOLVED); the division algorithm is NOT reconstructed (rule 5).
descriptors.provenance: OWN-MSL byte-diff (EXP-M4-13 R5): unsigned div/mod (`a/b`, `a%b`) emits `12 80 25 8b 22 81 85 00 20 80` (0x25 wide-select) and `12 02 2d 80 26 80 07 02 22 81` (0x2d correction select), 10B, cleanly bracketed by carry_gen. dst=byte0-hi from the family reg-sweep. NOT HW-dispatch validated.

descriptors.semantics: 2-byte compact low-nibble-2 helper `02 00` (dst r0, byte+1 == 0x00). A compiler-internal select/predicate/frame marker emitted between other ops (e.g. after a fence before a frame-marker, or between a subgroup-shuffle and an iadd). Distinct from the b_alu14_prep2 compact word (which has byte+1 bit0 == 1 and precedes a 0x83 b_alu14) and from the 6-byte iminmax (which carries a real op-select in byte+2). Length-only: a compiler-internal marshalling/predicate word, semantics deliberately NOT reconstructed (clean-room rule 5).
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R5 (own-MSL + corpus): appears as a standalone 2-byte word in transcendental/half/atan kernels (length 2 established by the byte0==0x02,byte+1==0x00 length rule; the following byte is the next op's head, which re-tokenizes cleanly). NOT HW-dispatch validated; op class inferred, not reconstructed.

descriptors.semantics: Generic 8-byte low-nibble-2 op (dst = byte0 high nibble), catch-all for the 8-byte forms that are NOT the register-operand SELECTs (isel8, byte+2 low3==7) nor the 0x25 isel_reg8. In practice this is the transcendental SFU RANGE-REDUCTION select (byte+1 == 0xc2, byte+2 in {0x19,0x29,0x49,0x59}, tail `.. 80 08`): a compiler-generated argument-reduction step feeding a polynomial evaluation. Length-classified only; per-op-select semantics UNRESOLVED and, for the SFU range-reduction selects, deliberately NOT reconstructed (clean-room rule 5).
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R5 catch-all. dst=byte0-hi from the family reg-sweep; length 8 from the low-nibble-2 length rule. byte fields captured for clean tokenization + round-trip; op semantics UNRESOLVED (SFU internal). NOT HW-dispatch validated.

descriptors.semantics: Generic 10-byte low-nibble-2 op (dst = byte0 high nibble), catch-all for the 10-byte forms not covered by the named selects (isel10/isel10_c/isel_reg/rt_transform_test). This bucket is a MIX: (a) the all-zero `X2 00 00 00 00 00 ..` word (dominant; a zero/pad select -- likely an OVER-READ of the byte0==0x22 default-to-10 length rule, see UNRESOLVED); (b) RAY-QUERY GETTER result-marshalling words (trailing `.. df 02 54 <off>` accel/ray-data load, or `.. 09 00 0f 06 04 01`, or `.. 67 81 10 02 00 80`) that read/pack a committed/candidate intersection field inside the intersection_query getters; (c) transcendental Horner/select steps (byte+2 0x08/0x0a/0x0c/0x10/0x12/0x14/0x16/0x18/0x1a/0x1c/0x1e). All are compiler-internal SFU / RT-getter marshalling; length-classified only, per-op semantics deliberately NOT reconstructed (rule 5).
descriptors.provenance: byte-diff EXP-M4-13 R5 catch-all. dst=byte0-hi from the family reg-sweep; length 10 from the low-nibble-2 length rule. RT-getter / SFU marshalling classification from corpus co-occurrence (these tokens appear only in intersection_query and transcendental kernels). byte fields captured for clean tokenization + round-trip; op semantics UNRESOLVED (compiler-internal). NOT HW-dispatch validated.

notes: PURELY ADDITIVE: instr_length() is UNCHANGED, so desync/tokenization is byte-identical to the committed DB (0 regression by construction). The 6 new descriptors only convert previously family-only low-nibble-2 tokens (lengths 2/8/10) into NAMED. Existing more-specific low-nibble-2 descriptors (iminmax, hminmax, isel_reg[0x2f], isel_reg8[0x25 8B], icmpsel, carry_gen, rt_transform_test, b_alu14_prep2, n2_op6) all have more match-bits and still win their signatures; verified 0 change to any existing decode. Match-bit design: isel8/isel10/isel10_c = 7 bits (group + byte+2 low-3-bits); catch-alls n2_op8/n2_op10 = 4 bits (group only); n2_compact2 = 16 bits (exact 02 00). The two 10-byte selects (isel10 low3==7, isel10_c low3==5) are mutually exclusive. CORE HW FACT (own-MSL PROVEN): byte+2 low-nibble {7,f}/{5,d} at this group is a register-operand compare-SELECT (dst=pred?srcA:srcB), NOT an integer multiply-add -- own MSL 'a*b+c' (int) emits the 12-byte 0x9f imad, while 'a>b?a:b' emits this low-nibble-2 SELECT. dst=byte0 high nibble (r0..r15), byte+1=srcA/size descriptor, byte+2=op/mode selector, byte+3=srcA, byte+4=srcB, wide forms append a trailing operand word at byte+8:9.
